english.title: With intent to deceive make / possess Swiss CPC / other document
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), with intent to deceive,

(A)_[made]_
(B)_[possessed]_

a document so closely resembling a

(C)_[Swiss Certificate of Professional Competence]_
(D)_[document issued to a driver by Switzerland certifying a Swiss initial Certificate of Professional Competence]_
(E)_[document issued to a driver by Switzerland certifying a Swiss periodic Certificate of Professional Competence]_

recognised by the competent authority as evidence of such for the purposes of regulation 11(2A) of the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007, as to be calculated to deceive
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 13(1)(c) and (4) of the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007.

english.notes:
(i) Being the holder of a certificate as required by the regulation may be evidenced by possession and production of any of the following:-
(a) a Swiss CPC; or
(b) any other document issued to the driver by Switzerland certifying a Swiss initial CPC or a Swiss periodic CPC and recognised by the competent authority as evidence of such for the purposes of this regulation, see regulation 11(2A).
(ii) In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, "forges" means makes a false document in order that it may be used as genuine.
(iii) See regulation 13(5), (6), (7) and (8) for details in relation to the time limits on prosecutions.
(iv) In relation to proceedings in Scotland, section 136(3) of the Criminal Procedure (Scotland) Act 1995 (date of commencement of proceedings) shall apply for the purposes of this regulation as it applies for the purposes of that section.
(v) See regulation 14 for the power to seize documents.
(vi) See offence H20127 for the offence of intent to deceive make / possess an authority / qualification card / community licence / certificate.
(vii) This offence no longer applies after the 2nd December 2024 due to changes made by SI 2024/1160 to the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007. For the offence applying after this date, see H101940.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit on prosecutions:
Complex - see regulation 13 of the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007.
